sentences.text: Macranhinga was an extinct genus of darters in the family Anhingidae that grew much larger than any other known fossil or living anhinga.
Individuals of this genus weighed between approximately 5.8 kg and 18.4 kg.
The largest members of the group likely lost the ability to fly entirely.
Evidence suggests they nested on the ground of small islands and islets, behaving similarly to modern large penguins.
The genus was originally described in 1992 by paleontologist Jorge Ignacio Noriega.
The type species M. paranensis was described based on complete tarsometatarsi and other skeletal parts.
Later, the genera Meganhinga and Giganhinga were found to be synonyms of Macranhinga, with Meganhinga having been described in 1995 for the species M. chilensis from Chile.
Researchers believe Macranhinga performed long, deep dives to catch large fish and prey.
The animal likely competed for food resources with dolphins, caimans, and seals.
Macranhinga fossils date from the Aquitanian to the Zanclean stages, between 23.04 and 5 million years ago.

Specimens of M. paranensis were found in the Ituzaingó Formation along the Paraná River in northeastern Argentina, where the species lived from the late Miocene to the early Pliocene in Entre Ríos province.
M. chilensis lived from the early to middle Miocene in central-southern Chile.
M. kiyuensis lived from the Pliocene to the middle Pleistocene in Uruguay.
M. ranzii lived from the late Miocene to the early Pliocene in Acre, Brazil, and Entre Ríos, Argentina.
